# The auto-lab, end to end: a per-endpoint issue inventory, and what was repaired

## What question this answers, and how it differs from the two shakedowns

The shakedowns asked *does the machinery work*. They answered yes — 154 of 161
ran clean, 286 dumps accepted, every checker verdict `complete: false` — and
that answer is not an issue inventory. It also concealed the state of the
corpus: 159 of 161 endpoints touched at most one declared target function and
39 touched none, and "ran clean" says nothing about either.

This run asks, for **each endpoint individually**: which stages ran and what
each returned; **where execution stopped and why**, as the real exception at
the real frame; what the dump contains; what the policy contains; and what is
wrong with any of it. Then it repairs what it found and measures the repair.

## How a stopping site is established

The shakedown's `concolic_terminal` carried `type`, `cause` and a 160-character
`message` and nothing about *where*. The driver now records, per RUN (including
runs whose dump was discarded as a duplicate path), the exception class, the
full message, `NameError#name`, `NameError#receiver.class`,
`ActionController::ParameterMissing#param`, the raising frame and the first 40
backtrace frames — all read off the live exception object inside the rescue,
never matched out of log text. `reports/autolab/entrypoints/lib/autolab_dse.rb`,
`terminal_record`.

Two endpoints are grouped under one issue only when they agree on
**(exception class, missing method name, receiver class, raising file:line)**.
A shared message is never sufficient: the inventory keeps
`UNMOCKED::NilClass#url_expires_in@…/blobs_controller.rb:11` and
`UNMOCKED::NilClass#url_expires_in@…/representations_controller.rb:11` apart,
because they are two call sites.

### One measurement in this directory was wrong, and is corrected rather than dropped

An early test appeared to show that killing a timed-out endpoint by process
group left two descendants alive, and a "fix" was written against it. It was
wrong: the check was `pgrep -f 'sleep 300'` run inside `bash -c`, whose own
command line contains the pattern, so it counted itself. Re-measured with
`exec -a` markers and a /proc scan (`scratchpad/pgtest3.py`), a cage'd parent
plus grandchild killed on timeout leaves **zero** survivors with the
process-group kill alone. The named-scope reaping was kept anyway — it makes an
in-flight endpoint visible in `systemctl --user list-units` and would cover a
stage that called `setsid` — but the docstring now records that the original
measurement was a false positive. This is exactly the error class the brief
warned about, caught in my own work.

## What changed about how the endpoints were driven, and why

**`MAX_RUNS` 2 → 24.** Not a preference: in the shakedown **125 of 161**
endpoints finished with `worklist_exhausted: false` and a non-empty worklist —
cut off by `MAX_RUNS`, not by the time budget and not by having nothing left to
explore. DSE itself cost **390.8 s across all 161 endpoints** (max 9.8 s each)
against roughly 180 s of JRuby+Rails boot *per endpoint*, so depth was nearly
free and the shallowness was a harness choice. What it changed, measured endpoint by endpoint against the shakedown's own
manifest — and stated exactly, because the obvious summary of it is wrong:

| endpoint | dumps | path conditions (richest dump) | reach |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aspect_memberships_create` | 2 → **23** | 16 → 16 | 10 → 10 |
| `comments_index` | 2 → **12** | 4 → **17** | 1 → **3** |
| `diaspora_federation_h_card_hcard` | 2 → **9** | 6 → 6 | 2 → 2 |
| `admin_pods_index` | 2 → 2 | 2 → 2 | 1 → 1 |

**Depth also widened the target surface the corpus touches at all.** Both
shakedowns reported the same **14** distinct target functions ever called
across 161 endpoints. Round 1 at `MAX_RUNS=24` reaches **16** — the two new
ones are `ActiveRecord::Relation#records` and
`ConcolicThroughLoadProbe.load_intermediate`, both on `comments_index`, both
only reachable on a path no 2-run exploration took. (And `#records` is the
target whose mock then raised `len_var_name`, which is how that defect was
found.)

So depth bought **distinct paths**, not always more decisions per path:
`aspect_memberships_create` already reached 16 path conditions in one dump at
`MAX_RUNS=2` and still does — what it gained is 21 more *distinct* paths
through them, and with them the two `AssociationTypeMismatch` runs and the 251
branches still on its worklist. Only `comments_index` gained path conditions
and reach as well. `admin_pods_index` gained nothing, because it dies at
`set_locale` either way. An endpoint that stops early has a small worklist and
empties it whatever MAX_RUNS is.

**Depth is also what found four of the defects below.** `len_var_name`
(FIX-7), the `SymbolicList#each` wall (FIX-9), the unscoped memo that refuses
five dumps (FIX-11) and the `AssociationTypeMismatch` on a gold endpoint were
all invisible at `MAX_RUNS=2`, because no endpoint got far enough to reach
them. "154 ran clean" was true and uninformative for the same reason.

**The gates are now asked, and answer NOT CONFIGURED.** The shakedown called
`run_complete(runs)` with no config at all, because `checks/shims.py:47` did
`config["extract_cmd"]` and raised `KeyError` on any config that named no shim
extractor. That was fixed in `src_new` on 2026-09-26, so this run passes
`CompletionConfig(batch_dir=…)` and each unconfigured step comes back `None`
with a blocking line naming it. A scaffolded endpoint genuinely has no shim
extractor, no audit command, no concrete run and no assumption driver, so NOT
CONFIGURED is the true state of its gates. **It is recorded as that state and
is not counted as a pass.**

**`run_complete` and `build_policy` now see every accepted dump**, not only the
highest-reach one. Passing a single dump made `coverage_complete: false` true by
construction and answered nothing about the endpoint.

# The issues, ranked by how many endpoints each blocks

The ranking below is derived from the per-endpoint records in
`INVENTORY.json`, not from a grep over logs. Each issue's `basis` field in
`INVENTORY_RANKED.json` states what evidence was used to group endpoints
under it; where that is weaker than a shared call site, the code says so.

## 1. The symbolic principal never resolved — 113 of 114 signed-in endpoints

**The stopping site, identical on all of them:**

```
NoMethodError: undefined method `language' for nil:NilClass
  receiver: nil (NilClass)   missing name: language
  raising frame:
    app/controllers/application_controller.rb:102:in `set_locale'
  called from:
    reports/autolab/entrypoints/lib/autolab_dse.rb:425:in `block in run_one'
```

**Why, established by executing the chain rather than reading it**
(`probes/probe_principal.out`):

| step | result |
|---|---|
| `User.to_adapter.get(uid)` | a symbolic `User` — the lookup DOES fire |
| `record.authenticatable_salt` | `SymbolicSubstring` of the **symbolic** `encrypted_password` column, concrete value `"SYM_RESULT_ActiveRecord__Find"` |
| `that == "concolicsalt"` | concrete **`false`** |
| `User.serialize_from_session(uid, "concolicsalt")` | **`nil`** |
| `current_user.language` | `NoMethodError` |

devise-4.7.1 `lib/devise/models/authenticatable.rb:238` keeps the record only
if `record.authenticatable_salt == salt`. The driver at `autolab_dse.rb:390`
resolves the principal with `User.serialize_from_session(ci_uid,
"concolicsalt")` — i.e. it already assumes a shim that makes that compare
true. That shim exists, in **one endpoint's** target layer
(`targets/endpoints/comments_index.rb`, "(a) salt leaf shim"; the same shim is
in `aspect_memberships_create.rb:1231-1239`). The shared core has none:
`User.ancestors` carrying `authenticatable_salt` are only the two real Devise
modules.

So every core-only signed-in endpoint resolved its principal to nil and died
in a `before_action` before the action body ran. That is the single largest
fact about this corpus, and "154 ran clean" did not contain it.

**Repaired** (FIX-1): the driver installs that leaf shim for candidate-tier
endpoints only. It is a `prepend`, not a `declare_target`, so the declaration
table is unchanged and the D5 double-declaration wrap cannot fire; an endpoint
with its own override installs its own and this never runs for one.

**Verified**: `probes/probe_fixes.out` — with the shim,
`serialize_from_session` returns a symbolic `User` and `current_user.language`,
`.gender` and `.person` all resolve.

## 2. The same defect also produced a malformed path condition and a silent UNSAT

The salt compare did not merely fail — it **recorded a path condition with no
symbolic operand**:

```json
{"op": "==", "args": [{"lit": {"sort": "str", "value": "SYM_RESULT_ActiveRecord__Find"}},
                      {"lit": {"sort": "str", "value": "concolicsalt"}}]}
```

recorded at `devise/models/authenticatable.rb:238`. Both sides are literals;
the left one is the symbolic `encrypted_password` column flattened to its
concrete prefix. Consequences, all observed:

* the endpoint reports **2** path conditions where **1** is real;
* the Z3 query does not parse —
  `Failed to parse constraint 'Not(And(…, Not(('SYM_RESULT_ActiveRecord__Find' == 'concolicsalt'))))': Context mismatch`
  (a Python `bool` inside a Z3 tree);
* and `concolic/solver.py:501-507` returns **UNSAT** for an unparseable
  constraint, so a branch that could not be *expressed* is reported as one
  that cannot be *taken*.

Root cause is `src_new/runtimes/ruby_runtime/term.rb:127-136`: a `SymbolicVar`
with no `sym_name` falls through to `lit(to_native(raw))`, and
`SymbolicSubstring#initialize` passes `name: nil`. Written up as **S-5** in
`findings/SRC_NEW_DEFECTS.md`; not repairable from here.

FIX-1 removes *this instance* (the salt compare becomes `String#==` against a
`ConcreteSymbolicString` and records nothing) — measured: `admin_pods_index`
went from 2 path conditions to 1. **The underlying defect is untouched** and
fires for any comparison against a nameless symbolic value.

## 3. `targets/core.rb` calls a runtime method that was deleted — every relation materialisation

```
NoMethodError: undefined method `len_var_name' for SymbolicVar:Module
  reports/autolab/targets/core.rb:1395:in `block in install!'
```

`SymbolicVar.len_var_name` was deleted from the runtime
(`src_new/runtimes/ruby_runtime/base.rb:33`, DESIGN_IR §4.1.1c change 3 —
"nothing replaces this method: there is no name to mint"), and
`runtimes/ruby_runtime/tests/test_name_boundary_seed.rb:116` asserts the
deletion. Two sites in `core.rb` still call it (1395, 1483), both only to
build a **seed key**. So `Relation#to_a` / `#to_ary` / `#records` raise.

**This is the clearest example of the shallowness hiding a defect.** No
shakedown endpoint reached it, because 113 of 161 died at `set_locale` first
and the rest stopped earlier. It surfaced within one run of the fix trial, as
soon as the principal resolved.

**Repaired** (FIX-7): the key is minted locally as `SYM_LEN_<var>`, the
spelling this file's own name boundary already documents and accepts
(`core.rb:98-124`, `length_var?`).

## 4. Gate 1b's representative row could not be reached

With FIX-7 in, the next wall is:

```
NotImplementedError: SymbolicList#each is not supported (contents out of scope)
  src_new/runtimes/ruby_runtime/list.rb:305
```

`core.rb:1386-1389` says the `records` mock attaches "a single representative
model row so SQL-free display/serialisation iteration COMPLETES" — but it
builds a plain `SymbolicList`, whose `each`/`map` are in `LIST_STUBS` and
raise. The representative existed and nothing could reach it. The library
already anticipates the answer 87 lines later: `core.rb:1482` reads
`defined?(IterableSymbolicList) ? IterableSymbolicList : SymbolicList`, and
that class exists only in `comments_index`'s layer.

**Repaired** (FIX-9): `core.rb:1395` takes the same lookup, and the driver
defines a minimal `IterableSymbolicList` for candidate endpoints, keeping both
of the gold version's load-bearing decisions (no `include Enumerable`, because
it would shadow the `any?`/`none?` that record `(len(X) != 0)`; and `map`
records the same compare as `each`, because a JSON render never compares the
length otherwise).

## 5. A "per-run" memo that outlives the run — 5 of one endpoint's 12 dumps refused

`comments_index` at `MAX_RUNS=24` has **5 of 12 dumps REFUSED** by
`validate_provenance`:

> symbol `SYM_RESULT_ActiveRecord__Relation_records_1_row_author_id` is an
> attribute of a value the dump types `obj<Comment>`, but the dump's type
> table declares no such type.

**Mechanism, measured rather than inferred** — the type table read out of every
dump the endpoint wrote:

| dump | calls `Relation#records` | type table | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| dse0001–0004, 0007, 0008 | no | `Post` / (none) | ok |
| **dse0005** | **yes — the first** | Comment, Mention, Person, Post, Profile | ok |
| dse0009, 0016, 0019, 0022, 0023 | yes | Person, Post[, Profile] — **no Comment** | **refused** |

The first materialisation declares `Comment`; every later one emits the same
41 `…records_1_row*` symbols and declares everything except it.
`comments_index.rb:968` memoises the list in
`Thread.current[:comments_rows_memo]`, and its own comment says the list is
memoised "for the life of the RUN" — but `Thread.current` belongs to the
process, one process drives every run, and a memo hit skips
`ct.symbolic_instance`, which is where `SymbolicFunc.register_type` fires,
while `save_and_clear_types` empties the table at every run boundary.

**Repaired** (FIX-11) with the guard `core.rb:1928-1933` already uses for the
`SingularAssociation` loaded-target memo: the cache resets when the run label
changes.

## 6. Six endpoints were reported as failures for doing what the design says

All six `build_policy` failures in both shakedowns were
`opaque reached the policy at: sig DeviseController#devise_mapping->returns`.
The check behind them (`shakedown/tools/pipeline.py:218 has_opaque`) was built
on `src_new/README.md:333` — "every `opaque` sits behind a `SHIM`, so none of
them can reach a policy". The second half does not follow from the first: a
shim is never an *access*, so it contributes no atom, but it does contribute a
*signature*, and a signature carries its declared return type.
`dumps_to_policy/normalize.py:341` says the same from the other side — "AN
ELIDED TARGET KEEPS ITS `sig` LINE, deliberately".

**Repaired** in `tools/pipeline.py` (`opaque_sites`), which separates entry
params and atom-referenced `target_function` returns — real defects — from
shim signature returns, which are by design. `sessions_new` now runs clean
through every stage.

The endpoints' *real* problem was elsewhere, and the backtrace names it:

```
NoMethodError: undefined method `authentication_keys' for #<Object:0x…>
  devise-4.7.1/lib/devise/parameter_sanitizer.rb:158:in `extract_auth_keys'
```

`core.rb:1998` has `def dev_stub.to(*_); self; end`, so `mapping.to` hands
Devise the **stub** where it expects the **model class**. Every method the six
died on — `authentication_keys`, `new_with_session`, `new`,
`reset_password_by_token`, `send_reset_password_instructions` — is a `User`
class method, and all five are present on `::User` (measured,
`probes/probe_fixes.out`). **Repaired** (FIX-2).

## 7. The SQL render produces nothing, for every endpoint in the corpus

Of the 73 endpoints the sweep had finished when this was measured, **72
render zero views**; their `.sql` files are a header and an EXCLUDED ATOMS
list. The reason recorded against each atom is:

```
the access note is not a SQL statement ({"refs": {"p0": "$SYM_USER_CI_id"}, "text": "SE…)
```

`domains/ruby_rails_sql/render.py:classify_note` takes the **first token of
the raw note string**, and §4.1.1c's note is a JSON envelope, so every
structured note classifies as `prose`. Proven in two lines:

```
classify_note('SELECT "posts".* FROM "posts" WHERE "posts"."id" = ?')       -> select
classify_note('{"refs": {"p0": "SYM_PARAM_post_id"}, "text": "SELECT …"}')  -> prose
classify_note(concolic.model.note.parse(<that envelope>).text)              -> select
```

The same file already knows this: `render.py:477-482` says "§4.1.1c's note
envelope is a JSON document, so a regex over the raw string would hand sqlglot
`{"refs": ...}` … `bind_split` is the one sanctioned reader". The *builder*
was taught to unwrap the envelope; the *capability predicate* that decides
whether the builder ever runs was not.

**The one endpoint that does render settles the cause.** `home_show` has
`views: 1` and `unsupported_atoms: 0`, and its single note is a PLAIN string —
`SELECT "roles".* FROM "roles" WHERE "roles"."name" = 'admin'` — because that
query has no binds, so the runtime wrote no envelope. It is the only note in
the corpus without one, and it is the only atom that renders. The note census
over the same 73 endpoints is 98 `select` + 16 `write` + **0 prose and 0
absent**: the notes are right, and one line of classification cannot read them.

Counting note SHAPES over every note in round 1 — 7 453 on symbolic vars and
events combined — gives **7 453 structured envelopes against 2 plain SQL
strings**. The envelope is not an edge case in this corpus; it is 99.97 % of
it, and one of the two plain notes is the one atom that renders.

Neither shakedown caught it because both measured SQL with their own parser in
`pipeline.py` and reported `render.sql_lines`, which counts a header the
renderer always writes. This is `src_new` and **not repairable from here** —
written up as **S-6**. The e2e pipeline now measures the cost instead:
`render.atoms_lost_to_note_envelope` re-asks the same classifier with the
payload unwrapped, so each endpoint records exactly how many atoms it loses to
that one line.

## 8. The document the review gates read has never described a real run

All 161 `config.json` files declare

```json
"scenarios": {"<variant>": {"MAX_RUNS": "6", "TIME_BUDGET": "600"}},
"limits": {"max_runs": 6}
```

Shakedown run 1 and run 2 both drove `MAX_RUNS=2, TIME_BUDGET=120`; this sweep
drives 24 / 300. `config.json` is not decoration — `concolic.review` quotes it
verbatim and the campaign digests it. A review item produced by the dry run
reads, in full:

> "Scenario 'auth_json' is selected by the environment
> [MAX_RUNS=6, TIME_BUDGET=600]. The claim is that this is one of the modes
> the endpoint really has, and that the set of scenarios is the whole set."

— a false statement about every run ever made from this config. Found by
running the campaign, not by reading the file.

**Repaired** (FIX-10) in two halves so it cannot recur silently: `sweep.py`
now takes the limits *from* each endpoint's `config.json` and records
`config_max_runs`, `config_time_budget` and `limits_overridden` on every
manifest row, and the configs are rewritten to the values actually driven.

## 9. The rig, not the application, decided three outcomes

Three stopping sites were the rig describing itself, recorded where the
endpoint's outcome belongs:

* **`Devise::MissingWarden`** (`sessions_create`, `sessions_destroy`). The rig
  dispatches the action directly and installs no Warden middleware, so
  `request.env['warden']` is nil and devise's accessor
  (`helpers.rb:142-144`) raises. That reads like an application fault and is
  not one. **FIX-6** replaces it with a named
  `AutolabDSE::AuthenticationRequired` that says so.
* **`Diaspora::NonPublic`** recorded as the terminal on `comments_index` and
  `likes_index` — while `comments_controller.rb:16` and
  `likes_controller.rb:15` both `rescue_from` it. The driver treated
  `rescue_with_handler` returning falsy as "no handler", collapsing "no
  handler matched" and "the handler itself raised" into one. (The handler is
  `{ authenticate_user! }`, which on an anonymous request reached the missing
  Warden.) **FIX-5** tells the two apart and records both.
  `reshares_index` has no `rescue_from`, so there the 500 is genuine.
* **`ActionView::Template::Error: couldn't find file 'underscore'`**
  (`home_show`, `home_podmin`, `streams_public`). The chain is
  `app/views/layouts/application.html.haml:11` → `javascript_include_tag :main`
  → `app/assets/javascripts/main.js:7` → `//= require underscore`, and the
  asset is absent because the application's own Gemfile header says so:
  *"Minimal Gemfile for concolic analysis — strips … frontend-only assets."*
  The tag is in the SHARED LAYOUT, so it sits on the path of every
  HTML-rendering endpoint and aborts the render before any query the template
  would issue. **FIX-12** stubs the two helpers in the rig only.

# What was NOT repaired, and why

Recorded in full in `findings/SRC_NEW_DEFECTS.md` (S-1…S-6, trees I may not
edit) and `findings/AUTOLAB_GAPS.md` (G-1…G-4, things I could have changed and
deliberately did not).

**In `src_new`, which a concurrent agent owns:**

* **S-1** `SymbolicString#include?` records the Z3 `Contains` operands
  **backwards** (`string.rb:179` passes the argument first; Z3's
  `Contains(a,b)` is "a contains b"). Not just cosmetic:
  `Contains("@", x) ∧ Length(x)=5` is **unsat** while the true predicate
  `Contains(x, "@") ∧ Length(x)=5` is **sat**, so a reachable branch looks
  infeasible. Corroborated inside the same file: `split` emits
  `IndexOf(suffix, sep)` — correct order — one line away from
  `Contains(sep, suffix)`.
* **S-2** `Contains(…)` is outside §7.2's sub-language, so `build_policy`
  refuses the whole dump. At `MAX_RUNS=24` this costs
  `diaspora_federation_h_card_hcard` **8 of its 9 dumps**, not one of two.
* **S-3** an unparseable constraint is returned as **UNSAT**.
* **S-5** a nameless symbolic value becomes a literal in the structured path
  condition (issue 2 above).
* **S-6** the SQL renderer classifies every structured note as prose (issue 7
  above).
* **S-4** `README.md:333`'s false invariant, which cost six endpoints in both
  shakedowns (issue 6 above).

**In the auto lab, left alone deliberately:**

* **G-1** the per-dump type table is **empty for all 159 candidate
  endpoints** — only the two gold layers install the `register_type` wrapper.
  Lifting it into the core is the right fix, but declaring a type turns
  `obj<?>` into a contract `validate_provenance` then enforces, and issue 5
  above is what that enforcement looks like when something else is subtly
  wrong. Turning it on for 159 endpoints in the same round as twelve other
  repairs would make any refusal impossible to attribute. It should be its own
  round.
* **G-3** `registrations_create` and the two `devise_passwords_*` writes need
  `params.require(:user)` — a **nested hash**. The scaffold's input model is
  flat symbolic strings, so this is a scaffold *design* change, not a missed
  scan; FIX-8 does not help.
* **G-4** the five ActiveStorage endpoints are not drivable and the lab is not
  why: there is no `config/storage.yml`, no environment sets
  `config.active_storage.service`, the app uploads with CarrierWave, and the
  routes exist only because `config/application.rb:5` is `require 'rails/all'`.
  `ActiveStorage::Blob.service` is nil in production too. They should be marked
  out of scope with that evidence, not mocked into existence.

**A gold endpoint's own modelling gap, surfaced by depth:**
`aspect_memberships_create` at 24 runs hits
`ActiveRecord::AssociationTypeMismatch: Aspect expected, got nil` at
`activerecord-5.2.4.3/lib/active_record/associations/association.rb:246`, from
`app/models/user/connecting.rb:21 share_with`, on 2 of 24 runs. It also ends
with **251 branches still on its worklist**. Both are for that batch's owner
to judge; neither is a harness fault.

# A cross-check worth stating

On `aspect_memberships_create` — the only endpoint deep enough to make the
arithmetic interesting — the three independent measurements agree exactly:

| measurement | value |
|---|---:|
| atoms after normalisation | 56 |
| atoms the SQL renderer excluded | 56 |
| access notes classified `select` (note census, P-5) | 41 |
| access notes classified `write` | 15 |
| atoms that WOULD render if the note envelope were unwrapped (P-4) | **41** |

41 + 15 = 56. The 15 writes are correctly not SELECT views (this endpoint
inserts an aspect membership); the 41 SELECTs are lost **entirely** to S-6's
one-line misclassification. The note census and the envelope probe are
computed from different objects by different code paths and land on the same
number, which is the check that neither is measuring itself.

Zero notes on this endpoint are prose and zero accesses carry no note, so
there is no "statement in a note that is wrong or missing" here — the notes
are right and the renderer cannot read them.

---

# Two things I got wrong, and what caught them

Both are recorded here rather than quietly corrected, because how a mistake
was caught is part of what the harness is worth.

**1. I edited the shared target library, and its own suite refused.** Four of
the repairs (FIX-2, FIX-7, FIX-9, FIX-11) were first applied as edits to
`targets/core.rb` and `targets/endpoints/comments_index.rb`. I had checked
each against both gold endpoints and concluded the blast radius was contained.
I had not checked the invariant that governs those files —
`test/test_install.rb:156-166`, "the library is byte-identical to the results4
gold it was copied from" — and the suite failed with `DRIFTED` on both. Both
files are reverted and byte-identical again; the same four repairs are now
made **from the runner** (`fixes/apply_runner_local_core_fixes.py`), which is
the technique the gold layers themselves name. The attempted versions are kept
as `*.e2e_attempt` for whoever decides whether the library's own copy should
change. Full account: `fixes/SHARED_BOUNDARY_DECISION.md`.

**2. My own new "failure" made two endpoints read as regressions.** P-3 flagged
a render that drops conditions as a failure, which flipped
`admin_pods_index` and `contacts_index` to `failed` in the round-2 trial even
though every stage returned `ok` and `contacts_index`'s reach had gone from 1
to **5**. The verification gate caught it as "verdict not worse: ran_clean ->
failed". A dropped condition is not even always a loss — the renderer drops a
predicate "the policy shows this shape running BOTH WITH AND WITHOUT", which
does not constrain it. `failures` now carry a `severity`, and only a
`stage`-severity failure decides the verdict; the quality findings are all
still recorded and all still reach the inventory.

**A third correction, of a fix rather than a claim.** FIX-12 was first written
as a stub of `javascript_include_tag` / `stylesheet_link_tag`, then widened to
the `*_path` family when `manifest_show` showed a second door
(`helpers.image_path`, no template at all). The verification trial found a
third: `sprockets-rails-3.2.1/lib/sprockets/rails/helper.rb:135` overrides
`javascript_include_tag` and, under `request_debug_assets?`, reaches Sprockets
through `lookup_debug_asset` **without going through `compute_asset_path`**.
Stubbing helpers one at a time was chasing doors, so the fix now answers the
five-method Sprockets seam instead and leaves every tag helper alone. After
it, `home_show`, `home_podmin` and `streams_public` stop at
`SymbolicString#gsub` — a genuine runtime boundary, reached further in.

---

# Where the stops LIVE — a one-line summary of round 1

Each endpoint's dominant stopping site, bucketed by which tree the raising
frame is in (measured over the endpoints finished at the time of writing):

| where the raising frame lives | endpoints |
|---|---:|
| the application's own source | 67 |
| no unrescued exception at all | 15 |
| a gem (ActiveStorage, Devise, ActionPack) | 11 |
| the symbolic runtime (`NotImplementedError`) | 4 |
| JRuby internals (`CGI.unescape`) | 2 |
| **the target library** | **0** |

The zero is worth noticing. The mocks themselves never raised in round 1 —
and yet `targets/core.rb:1395` raises `NoMethodError` on *every* relation
materialisation (FIX-7). It never fired because no round-1 endpoint got far
enough to materialise one. **That is the shape of this whole corpus**: the
library's own defects are invisible behind the wall that stops execution
before the library is used, which is why FIX-7 and FIX-9 had to land in the
same round as FIX-1 rather than after it.

---

# What the corpus actually records, at round 1

Measured directly from every dump the round-1 sweep wrote (the note payload
unwrapped, then classified by its first token):

| statement | occurrences | endpoints recording at least one |
|---|---:|---:|
| `SELECT` | 451 | **66** |
| `INSERT` | 24 | **1** |
| `UPDATE` | 22 | **1** |
| `DELETE` | 1 | **1** |

Tables touched, by occurrence: `users` 175, `blocks` 72, `people` 66,
`contacts` 48, `aspect_memberships` 34, `aspects` 31, `profiles` 26, `posts`
16, `notifications` 12, `comments` 6, `mentions` 6, `authorizations` 3,
`o_auth_applications` 2, `roles` 1.

Two things to read off this rather than past it. **`users` dominates because
it is the principal lookup** — the one query most signed-in endpoints manage
before they die, not evidence of endpoint behaviour. And **the entire write
surface of this corpus is two endpoints**, `aspect_memberships_create` and
`api_openid_connect_authorizations_destroy`, exactly as both shakedowns found;
raising the depth multiplied the *occurrences* (2 dumps became 23) without
reaching a single new writing endpoint.

# Where I am uncertain, stated rather than papered over

Each of these is a place where I have evidence for *what* happens and not for
*why*, or where I made a judgement that someone closer to the modelling should
check. None of them is presented above as settled.

1. **The three-arm `users.language` domain (FIX-3) applied to ~113 endpoints.**
   I did not re-derive it. It is copied from the two gold batches, whose own
   comment argues it is app-wide because the two callbacks live in
   `ApplicationController` and every signed-in endpoint runs them — and I
   checked that the callbacks are indeed there. But the domain itself ("pl"
   available-and-inflected / "xx" not-available / "en" available-not-inflected)
   came out of an adversary round on *one* endpoint. If it is wrong, it is
   wrong on every candidate endpoint at once.

2. **`Diaspora::NonPublic` on `reshares_index`.** I established that
   `reshares_controller.rb` has no `rescue_from` for it while
   `comments_controller` and `likes_controller` do, so the exception is
   genuinely unrescued there. I did **not** establish what production does
   with it — an unrescued `StandardError` is a 500 either way, but what the
   pod actually serves is not something this harness measures.

   **One half of this I was able to settle, and did.** The launcher's header
   flags that `concolic_mod.rb:33` keeps `consider_all_requests_local = true`
   where `production.rb:17` has `false`, and warns that this "matters to the
   scaffolds' generic terminal policy". Read through, it does not: the flag is
   consumed in exactly one place,
   `railties-5.2.4.3/lib/rails/application.rb:255`, where it seeds
   `env["action_dispatch.show_detailed_exceptions"]` for the
   `ActionDispatch::DebugExceptions` middleware — it decides how an error page
   is RENDERED, not whether an exception is raised and not which `rescue_from`
   runs (`actionpack/lib/action_controller/metal/rescue.rb:21-25` calls
   `rescue_with_handler(exception) || raise` unconditionally). The rig
   dispatches the action directly, so no middleware runs at all and the driver
   calls `rescue_with_handler` itself. **The flag is inert for everything this
   harness records.** The residual gap noted in the launcher can be closed.

3. **Whether the federation receive endpoints proceed once `:xml` is
   symbolic.** I established the cause of the stop precisely —
   `CGI.unescape(params[:xml])` with `params[:xml]` nil, at
   `receive_controller.rb:48`, because the param is read in a private helper
   the scaffold never scanned — and FIX-8 will make the param symbolic. I have
   **not** verified that `CGI.unescape` accepts a `SymbolicString`; it may
   simply move the stop one line. That will be visible in the next sweep and I
   have not pre-judged it.

4. **The five `SymbolicString` `NotImplementedError` sites** (`downcase`,
   `=~`, `strip`, `gsub!`, `split` with a multi-character separator). These are
   declared scope limits of the runtime, not bugs, and each is reached from a
   different application line. Whether each can be answered by a target at the
   smallest enclosing SQL-free method — the discipline the gold batches use —
   is a per-endpoint judgement I did not make for any of them.

5. **What `MAX_RUNS` should actually be.** 24 is measured to be enough for 49
   of the 52 endpoints that had finished when I checked, and measured to be far
   too small for the other three (`aspect_memberships_create` ends with 251
   branches on its worklist, `comments_index` with 59). I do not know the right
   value for the deep ones and did not search for it; what I did instead is
   make `stack_remaining` and `worklist_exhausted` visible per endpoint so the
   need is legible, and make the limit come from each endpoint's own config
   rather than from a flag (FIX-10), so it can differ per endpoint.

6. **`EXHAUSTED_BEHIND_A_WALL` is the honest reading of most "exhausted"
   endpoints, and I cannot quantify what is behind the wall.** An endpoint that
   dies at an unmocked call has a small worklist and empties it; reporting
   `worklist_exhausted: true` for it is true and deeply misleading. The
   inventory separates the two, but neither I nor the artifacts can say how
   many branches lie past the wall until the wall is gone.
